title: Hy Clark's Missourians at the Savoy and admiring Chick Webb
summary: He joins Hy Clark's second-rate Savoy band, develops, and Chick Webb, whom he rates as the best bandbuilder, listens to him.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: So there was a little band in the Palladium -- in the Savoy called the Hy Clark and his Missourians. They need a trumpet. And when I went there, they give me the job. It was a second-rate orchestra. But that's when I really got developed.
Was this a kind of an opening band (inaudible)?

It was one of those second-rate bands. They used them at the Savoy as a (inaudible) band, you know, so that chance to develop my playing and got better experience with the jazz and listen all these good men they used to play in there, those bass. You know what I mean? So I'm ready for everybody. So I practiced with that band around six or seven months. Chick Webb Cheat-Wook (phonetic) was working there all the time, in and out, in and out, in and out. So he used to listen to me. I don't have no idea I'm ever going to play with the -- because he always had you have the best in business and the bestest, and to me up to today I don't think there has been anybody better -- with better idea how to form an orchestra, how to play than him. He was (inaudible) musician because he got -- he got an ear, he had a conception about rhythm and the arrangement, how to play. There was nothing like it. For me there was nothing like it. So we had a trumpet player called Lou Bacon
